title: Generalized Copernicus–Euler Problem on the Complex Spheroid. Part 1. The First Law of Tectonic Motion
content: This article presents a new kinematic model of the Earth's rotation, derived from solving the generalized Copernicus-Euler problem for a deformable spheroid. For the first time, tectonic motions of the Earth's surface are described as orbits of the conformal Möbius group action on a complex spheroid. It is shown that any observed surface motion can be decomposed into a composition of four elementary rotations, unifying astronomical motions (polar motion, rotation variations) and tectonic deformations into a single mathematical model. A crucial aspect is that this description requires no a priori assumptions about the Earth's internal structure or composition. By analogy with Kepler's first law, the First Law of Tectonic Motion is formulated, establishing the geometric invariants of tectonic processes. An analysis of the current state of tectonics as a science reveals the need to correct its methodological foundations, and the proposed model sets a new direction for development, returning it to the realm of fundamental physics and geometric group theory.
